review_items.title: 'List increase' proposed as the realised price for the January 2027 cycle - treat a proposed list change as price?
review_items.detail: The working proposal assumes the full 5.0% is realised on every channel. The October 2025 list was realised at 92% through dealers and 0% at OEM for eleven months; BuildMart is fixed to March and HomeBase is capped at 6%. Accepting the proposal would make 'price' mean 'list' in every answer that names the cycle.

pivot.title: 'List increase' proposed as the realised price for the January 2027 cycle - treat a proposed list change as price?
pivot.detail: The working proposal assumes the full 5.0% is realised on every channel. The October 2025 list was realised at 92% through dealers and 0% at OEM for eleven months; BuildMart is fixed to March and HomeBase is capped at 6%. Accepting the proposal would make 'price' mean 'list' in every answer that names the cycle.
pivot.why_pivot: This item changes what a word means, not what a row says. Accepting it silently would make every answer about the January cycle report list as price, and the increase needed to hold the floor would be understated on the fixed and capped channels.

nodes.label: ProductFamily
nodes.sublabel: A product family: the grain at which margin, target and price action resolve.

nodes.label: Plant
nodes.sublabel: A manufacturing plant or distribution centre. Capacity without code-report coverage cannot ship.

nodes.label: Supplier
nodes.sublabel: A supplier of steel, components, finished goods or services.

nodes.label: SupplierContract
nodes.sublabel: An executed supply agreement with its price-change, pass-through and fixed-price terms.

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.sublabel: A customer: national account, builder, dealer, co-op or OEM.

nodes.label: CustomerAgreement
nodes.sublabel: A customer agreement whose clauses govern notice, caps and qualifying costs.

nodes.label: Clause
nodes.sublabel: A contract clause that sets a rule: notice, share, cap, qualifying cost.

nodes.label: Condition
nodes.sublabel: A dated condition that qualifies a clause or a decision.

nodes.label: PriceAction
nodes.sublabel: A list or contract price change with its effective date and scope. A proposal is not a price.

nodes.label: CustomsEntry
nodes.sublabel: An entry filed by the broker, with its duty lines and its mill certificate present or missing.

nodes.label: DutyLine
nodes.sublabel: A duty program line on an entry: IEEPA, Section 301, Section 232 steel content.

nodes.label: MillCertificate
nodes.sublabel: A mill test certificate: country of melt and pour and heat numbers.

nodes.label: RefundDeclaration
nodes.sublabel: A refund declaration for IEEPA duty in one of four states.

nodes.label: SupplierNotice
nodes.sublabel: A supplier's price notice; valid only after the contract's notice period.

nodes.label: SupplierInvoice
nodes.sublabel: A supplier invoice; its price can differ from the notice and the PO.

nodes.label: CodeReport
nodes.sublabel: An evaluation report listing products and the plants qualified to make them.

nodes.label: InspectionRequest
nodes.sublabel: A request to the evaluation agency to list a plant; only a revised report is coverage.

nodes.label: ChangeRequest
nodes.sublabel: A plant move or supplier change under change control, gated by the code report.

nodes.label: BuilderProgram
nodes.sublabel: A rebate program paid on confirmed dealer sell-through files.

nodes.label: SteelGrade
nodes.sublabel: A steel grade with its index, cover and exposure.

nodes.label: SteelIndex
nodes.sublabel: A published steel price index.

nodes.label: Statement
nodes.sublabel: A dated claim made in a document or a message - evidence, never a record by itself.

nodes.label: Measure
nodes.sublabel: A governed measure with a named definition, grain and date basis.

nodes.label: Gross margin by family
nodes.sublabel: net sales − cost of sales (steel, duty, freight, conversion, other) ÷ net sales, per certified month

nodes.label: Landed cost per pound
nodes.sublabel: supplier price + duty at the entry-date rate + inbound freight, ÷ net weight, per source

nodes.label: Price realisation
nodes.sublabel: net invoice price ÷ list price in force, per channel and family

nodes.label: Tariff cost per family
nodes.sublabel: duty recognised in cost of sales per family, as inventory turns

nodes.label: Recoverable pass-through
nodes.sublabel: supplier's share of new duties under a pass-through clause, within window and cap

nodes.label: Weeks of steel cover
nodes.sublabel: tons on hand ÷ trailing 8-week consumption, per grade; tons on order shown separately

nodes.label: Rebate accrual
nodes.sublabel: confirmed sell-through × tier reached year to date; no file, no estimate

nodes.label: Recoverable duty
nodes.sublabel: IEEPA duty on entries to 20 Feb 2026, by state: refunded, claimed, unclaimed

nodes.label: Protected revenue share
nodes.sublabel: share of net sales under agreements whose price cannot change before a stated date

nodes.label: Cost coverage ratio
nodes.sublabel: qualifying cost increase ÷ revenue effect of a price increase, per agreement

nodes.label: Notice-window days remaining
nodes.sublabel: days until a notice or claim deadline set by a clause

nodes.sublabel: share of a family's code reports that list a plant

sanity_checks.question: Which product families are below target gross margin this quarter, and by how much?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - at family grain, certified months only
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is ProductFamily -> margin by certified month -> target from the pricing policy. Open months are excluded. The floor is tested once at company level, not per family (rq5).
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (f:ProductFamily)-[:HAS_MEASURE]->(m:Measure {id:'gm_by_family'})
MATCH (m)-[:TESTED_AGAINST]->(c:Condition {id:'gm_floor'})
RETURN f, m, c

sanity_checks.question: Why did Ningbo Kaitong raise its price in September, and does the invoice match what they told us?
sanity_checks.verdict_body: Supplier -> SupplierNotice -> Clause 7.2 (45 days) resolves the valid date; SupplierInvoice CONTRADICTS the notice on the rate. The reason is the supplier's claim; whether clause 7.2 was breached is not decided by the graph.
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (s:Supplier {id:'ningbo_kaitong'})-[:ISSUED]->(n:SupplierNotice)-[:TESTED_AGAINST]->(c:Clause {id:'sa_7_2'})
MATCH (i:SupplierInvoice)-[:CONTRADICTS]->(n)
RETURN s, n, c, i

sanity_checks.question: What increase does the HomeBase cost justification support, and by when must we serve notice?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - lines evaluated, one cannot be
sanity_checks.verdict_body: CustomerAgreement -> §12.3 defines qualifying costs; each cost line resolves to a record or not. The four entries without a mill certificate make one line 'cannot evaluate' (rq3). Notice date derives from §12.1.

sanity_checks.question: If we move 40% of anchor volume to Lebanon, what do we save, and which code reports must list the plant first?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - saving and gate, not timing
sanity_checks.verdict_body: ChangeRequest -> landed cost resolves the saving; ChangeRequest GATED_BY InspectionRequest -> CodeReport resolves the gate. NES's schedule is not connected, so the timing is a stated indication (rq4).
sanity_checks.plan:

MATCH (cr)-[:TESTED_AGAINST]->(m:Measure {id:'landed_cost'})
RETURN cr, ir, r, m

story_group.story: Ridgeline Structural Products makes connectors, truss plates, fasteners, adhesives and shearwalls at Tracy and Lebanon and buys anchors, tools and wire from suppliers in China, Taiwan and Mexico. Margin is reported per product family per certified month, with cost of sales split into steel, duty, freight, conversion and other; October is open and never read. The company floor is 47.0% gross margin (20% operating) and each family carries a target. A price action has an effective date and a scope; a proposed one is not a price, and a list change is realised only when net ÷ list holds. Customer agreements carry notice periods, caps, qualifying-cost clauses and fixed terms; supplier contracts carry notice days, pass-through shares with windows and caps, and fixed-price lots. A customs entry carries duty lines by program and a mill certificate; without the certificate the steel-content line is unevidenced. Refund declarations have four states that are never summed. A code report lists the plants qualified to make a family; capacity at a plant not listed cannot ship. A supplier's notice, a buyer's email and a dealer's estimate are statements, never records.

grain.Margins: one product family x plant x month
grain.Duty_Lines: one entry x duty program line

uncertainties: margin_monthly.cogs_duty_usd is recognised as inventory turns; it never reconciles to duty_line in the same month.
supplier_price_notice.valid_from depends on the clause's notice days; a supplier with two contracts needs the clause picked by family.
plant_capacity.qualified is maintained by hand; it should derive from code_report_plant.status = Listed.
agreement_term.value_num is null for text-only terms (qualifying costs); the clause text is the rule.
dealer_sell_through is the builder's purchases from the dealer, not RSP's invoices; the two must not be joined.
duty_line.chapter99_code is null on 14 lines where the declaration was rejected.

type_links.reason: Documents name families by the same names the margin table is keyed on (family_code).
Entry ids in documents match customs_entry keys.
Supplier invoice numbers in documents match supplier_invoice_line.invoice_no.
Contracts carry the clauses the terms cite; a contract is not itself a term row.
Agreement ids in documents match customer_agreement keys.
clause_ref on the term points at the clause.
clause_ref on the term points at the clause.
Conditions qualify a term (cap, notice, qualifying cost).
Report plants belong to a report.
A plant is listed on a report, or not.
An inspection request is the status of a plant on a report, not a listing.
Amounts in documents may be duty, invoice totals or caps - only the basis tells which.
A quoted amount is not a certified margin figure.
A percent in a document (notice rate, cap) is not a margin.
Caps and rates are term values.
Organisations are parties to agreements.
Suppliers named in documents may match po_line.supplier_id via the supplier register.
Exporters named on entry summaries match customs_entry.supplier_id.
People are named as signatories or buyers; personal data, masked for analysts.
A date in a document is not an invoice date unless the ERP records it.
Effective, renewal and deadline dates bound terms.
Cities locate plants; a city is not a listing.
Duty lines belong to an entry.
An invoice is against a PO line; its price can differ.
A person is not a party to a supplier contract; the organisation is.
An inspection has no margin meaning.
